Launch: INFINITO v0.5 on Bemula-Lite, once.

Approved by the maintainer on 2026-11-03. Bemula-Lite: 31 instances, 62 forget
requests, 848 questions (github.com/Nboxff/bemula-benchmark at 862aff6). None
of it was used to develop or calibrate v0.5: that used only the 19 other
instances of the full benchmark.

Configuration, fixed before the run and chosen on the development instances:
INFINITO stores what the user says, recognizes forget requests with rules,
plans them with gpt-5.6-luna reviewing every memory in batches of 60, and
deletes the chosen rows with the history of their facts. Questions get the
16 most relevant memories, without pruning, under 3,000 tokens. Answers use
Bemula's RAG prompt with gpt-5.6-luna (reasoning none); the judge is
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at temperature 0, as in the paper's GPT-5.6-Luna runs;
embeddings text-embedding-3-small.

Comparison: Bemula's published GPT-5.6-Luna runs (Naive RAG, Mem0, A-MEM,
LangMem, LightMem, SimpleMem, Full Context), recomputed on the same 31
instances. Best Bemula Score among them: A-MEM, 26.3. Requests passed end to
end: 0 of 62 for every one of them.

Decision rule, fixed before the run: INFINITO's forgetting is called better
than every published system if its Bemula Score is above 26.3 and it passes
at least one forget request end to end. Retention, preservation and
relearning are reported alongside. Whatever the outcome, it is reported as
found.

Models are called through OpenAI's and DeepSeek's own APIs (Bemula's runs used
an OpenAI-compatible gateway), so Bemula's token limit reaches GPT-5 as
max_completion_tokens. The development check that preceded this run (Actions
run 41616879384, 4 development instances) ran the whole pipeline with these
models; nothing was changed after it.
